results.label: Kant, Kritik der reinen Vernunft — philosophy, hard

results.label: Fontane, Effi Briest — narrative, long sentence
results.de: In den letzten Novembertagen des Jahres 1859, eines Nachmittags, den man noch zum Fahrradfahren hätte benutzen können, ging in Berlin, in der alten Keithstraße, ein Herr von mittlerer Größe und militärischem Aussehen von der Treppe eines Vorderhauses hinab auf die Straße.

argos.text: In the last days of November 1859, an afternoon which could still have been used for cycling, a gentleman of medium size and military appearance walked down the stairs of a front house in Berlin, in the old Keithstraße.

nllb.text: In the last days of November 1859, an afternoon that could still have been used for cycling, a gentleman of medium size and military appearance went down the stairs of a front house on the street in Berlin, in the old Keithstraße.

results.label: Kafka, Die Verwandlung — famous opening
results.de: Als Gregor Samsa eines Morgens aus unruhigen Träumen erwachte, fand er sich in seinem Bett zu einem ungeheueren Ungeziefer verwandelt.

argos.text: When Gregor Samsa woke up one morning from troubled dreams, he found himself transformed into a monstrous vermin in his bed.

nllb.text: When Gregor Samsa woke up one morning from restless dreams, he found himself in his bed transformed into an enormous insect.

nllb.text: The Panther in the Jardin des Plantes, Paris: his gaze is so tired of the passing of the rods that he holds nothing.

results.label: SYNTHETIC — long paragraph, ~80 words
results.de: Die Geschichtsschreibung des neunzehnten Jahrhunderts hat lange geglaubt, dass der Fortschritt eine gerade Linie sei. Aber wer die Briefe der Beteiligten liest, bemerkt schnell, dass fast jede Entscheidung unter Zeitdruck getroffen wurde, dass die Akteure oft nicht wussten, welche Folgen ihre Handlungen haben würden, und dass der spätere Sieger meist nicht der war, der am besten geplant hatte, sondern der, der am schnellsten aus Fehlern lernte. So gesehen ist jede große Erfindung auch ein Bericht über das Scheitern der Alternativen.

argos.text: The historiography of the nineteenth century has long believed that progress is a straight line. But those who read the letters of the participants quickly realize that almost every decision was made under time pressure, that the actors often did not know what consequences their actions would have, and that the later winner was usually not the one who had planned best, but the one who learned the fastest from mistakes. In this sense, every great invention is also a report on the failure of alternatives.

nllb.text: Nineteenth-century historians have long believed that progress was a straight line. But if you read the letters of those involved, you quickly notice that almost every decision was made under time pressure, that the actors often didn't know what the consequences of their actions would be, and that the subsequent winner was usually not the one who had the best plans, but the one who learned the fastest from mistakes.
